data.title: Middle East Eye: Resolution demanding accountability for Americans killed by Israel fails in US Senate
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Resolution demanding accountability for Americans killed by Israel fails in US Senate
A resolution demanding answers on Israel's killing of US citizens in the occupied West Bank failed to gain Senate approval late on Tuesday, after just 47 lawmakers voted in its favour.
Among them was the lone Republican, Kentucky Senator Rand Paul.
One Democrat, Pennsylvania Senator John Fetterman, joined 50 other Republicans to vote against it.
Republicans Bill Cassidy of Louisiana and Dan Sullivan of Alaska did not vote in the 100-member upper chamber.
Maryland Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen, a vocal supporter of Palestinian rights and curbing US aid to Israel, introduced Senate Resolution 852 earlier this month, pursuant to Section 502(b) of the Foreign Assistance Act, which allows lawmakers to request human rights reports from the State Department on countries that receive US assistance.
Read more: Resolution demanding accountability for Americans killed by Israel fails in US Senate

data.title: Middle East Eye: Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Hegseth says American forces have ‘destroyed’ Iran’s military
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth told a gathering of military leaders at Quantico Marine base on Wednesday that US forces have “destroyed” Iran’s navy, air force, defence systems, leadership and military-industrial capacity.
Hegseth praised the American troops he addressed, crediting them with having destroyed Iran’s “entire defense space”.
“Iran’s conventional shield has been crippled, and their nuclear ambitions have been crippled and laid bare for the world,” he added.
Hegseth said the Pentagon has undergone a “clear break” from its past, with a “singular mission” of war-fighting. He said the department had fired “nearly 10 percent of the generals and admirals across the force”, a figure he framed as “accountability” rather than a “purge”, as some media have called it.
US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth gives an address at Marine Corps Base Quantico, on 30 September 2026 (Alex Wong/AFP)

data.title: Middle East Eye: Wisconsin Palestinian community leader can be deported, immigration judge rules
data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
Wisconsin Palestinian community leader can be deported, immigration judge rules
A US immigration judge ruled on Wednesday that Salah Sarsour, a Muslim and Palestinian community leader in his hometown of Milwaukee, Wisconsin, can be deported per the wishes of the Trump administration.
In a press briefing following the decision, his lawyer, Patrick Taurel, confirmed that he will appeal.
For the time being, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) cannot re-detain Sarsour because a federal judge's order ensuring he walks free remains in place.
As with a number of Palestinian Green Card holders before Sarsour, such as former Columbia University students Mahmoud Khalil and Mohsen Mahdawi, as well as the Georgetown University scholar Badar Khan Suri, who is married to a Palestinian American, the US government arrested Salah in March on the grounds that he is a threat to national security.
His legal team and advocates maintain the arrest was because of his speech in defence of Palestinian rights. Sarsour sits on the board of American Muslims for Palestine (AMP), which pro-Israeli groups have claimed is a front for Hamas.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday rejected UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham's claim that Iran "played a part" in a suspected attempted attack on RAF Fairford, a British base used by the US to conduct its war on Iran.
"I can confirm Iran's belief that releasing supposed terrorists working for foreign states really says it all," Araghchi said in a post on X, referring to the five suspects being released on bail by counter-terror police shortly after the incident.
"You're barking up the wrong tree," he added.
PM Burnham says the UK Government "can confirm our belief that we believe Iran to have played a part" in the RAF Fairford incident.

data.author: Fleur Hargreaves
data.summary:
US representatives introduce bill sanctioning expanding Israeli settlements
A growing number of Democratic lawmakers are ramping up pressure on Israel, introducing legislation to impose sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank and Gaza.
The Stop the Settlements Act, led by Representatives Joaquin Castro, Madeleine Dean, Don Beyer, Greg Casar, Sara Jacobs and Veronica Escobar, would block new settlement construction or expansion through sanctions and a ban on importing goods made in settlements and outposts.
“Under Netanyahu’s government, settlers are engaged in a violent land grab that’s ripping Palestinians from their land. Sanctions can help stop it,” US Representative Joaquin Castro wrote in a post on X.
